nodes.question: In the edited image, can the source-image paper and cup be identified, and is that paper visibly stuffed inside that cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the edited image provides enough visual evidence to identify the same paper and cup shown in the source and shows the paper placed inside the cup with evidence it has been stuffed into it. Fail only if both objects are identifiable and the paper is visibly outside the cup or merely on its rim. Unknown if either object's identity, or their placement, cannot be established.
nodes.binding: Anchor “the paper” and “the cup” to the objects in the source image. Do not treat a visually different-looking item or object in the edited image as the same object without sufficient evidence.

nodes.question: In the edited image, can the source-image paper and cup be identified, and is there visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup without the paper already being stuffed inside?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the edited image provides enough evidence to identify the same paper and cup shown in the source, shows movement or placement advancing the paper toward or into the cup, and s1 has not established completion. Fail only if both objects are identifiable and there is visibly no progress toward the requested placement, or s1 establishes completion. Unknown if either object's identity or the relevant progress relation cannot be established.
nodes.binding: Progress counts only when it advances stuffing the source-image paper into the source-image cup. Do not infer absence of progress from uncertain object identity or proximity.

nodes.question: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
nodes.criteria: Return yes when support 1 passes: the requested outcome is visibly complete. Return no only when support 1 fails and support 2 fails, establishing that no requested change has progressed. Return partial when support 1 fails and support 2 passes, establishing some progress without completion. Return unknown whenever the evidence needed to distinguish these alternatives is unresolved. A skipped support is unobserved, not automatically inapplicable; on any skipped path, return a decision only if the remaining evidence establishes that same outcome under the rubric, otherwise return unknown. Supporting evidence earns no completion credit independently, and unrelated edits do not count as progress.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague: “paper (...) stuffed into the cup” omits the source-to-edit identity and the distinction between completion and partial progress. Make the typed criteria explicitly assess whether the edited scene shows the source paper and cup (allowing reasonable appearance changes), whether the paper is visibly inserted into the cup, and whether any identifiable part of the requested action has progressed without completion. Here, the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a reddish object; it does not visibly establish the source paper or blue cup, insertion, or progress. That is unresolved visual evidence—not proof that no change occurred—so do not force the reference “no” by relaxing the rubric or treating unidentifiable objects as absent. The high-confidence unresolved judgments warrant checking whether the evidence prompts support calibrated identity matching and partial-progress assessment. The trace is valid and queried, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure indicated; preserve the existing completion/no-progress/partial/unknown logic and improve the binding’s evidence criteria rather than changing routing or adding dependencies.
s2: The trace is valid and queried, so this is not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. The binding already names source-to-edit identity and warns against inferring no progress from uncertain identity; the downstream diagnosis that it omits these distinctions does not match the supplied node. Avoid weakening the rubric or forcing the reference label. Instead, make the typed criteria operational for visual comparison: allow reasonable appearance changes while requiring affirmative cues that the edited item is the source paper and the nearby object is the source cup, and distinguish visible movement or placement toward insertion from mere proximity or an unrelated hand-held item. In these images, the source shows white paper and a blue cup, while the edit shows a blue printed item near a reddish object; identity and action progress are not established, so unknown is appropriate—not evidence of no change. Investigate why a high-confidence judgment remains unresolved and whether the evidence prompt supports calibrated identity matching and partial-progress assessment. Preserve completion, no-progress, partial, and unknown logic; do not add dependencies or alter routing.
s1: The binding already anchors the paper and cup to the source image, so do not repeat the inaccurate diagnosis that it omits source-to-edit identity. The trace is valid and queried; there is no transport, schema, or dependency failure. The images show a white sheet and blue cup in the source, versus a hand-held blue printed item near a reddish object in the edit. Neither object identity nor insertion/progress is established, so the unresolved result is appropriate; the reference “no” is not atomic ground truth and does not justify forcing a negative or treating uncertain objects as absent. Improve the typed criteria only where needed: allow reasonable appearance changes but require affirmative visual cues for identity, and distinguish actual movement/placement toward insertion from mere proximity. Preserve completion, no-progress, partial, and unknown distinctions and existing routing/dependencies. Investigate the high-confidence unresolved judgment by checking whether the evidence prompt supports calibrated identity matching and partial-progress assessment; do not interpret confidence or repeated variation as proof that an edit is absent.

semantic_rejection.reason: The saved fulfillment alternatives do not preserve the rubric’s progress/endpoint meaning. They make s1 fail a prerequisite for both “no” and “partial,” although s1 can be unknown when completion is insufficiently evidenced; that leaves known progress or known absence of progress unresolved. They also make s3 required even though the saved alternatives say it cannot affect the label, so an unresolved s3 can block a result that the rubric permits from other evidence.
semantic_rejection.counterexample: If s1 is unknown, s2 pass establishes progress short of completion, but the fulfillment criteria require s1 fail for partial, so the known partial result is lost. If s1 is unknown and s2 fail establishes no progress, the criteria likewise prevent the rubric’s “no” result. Conversely, s1 pass establishes completion, but required s3 unknown can leave fulfillment unresolved despite the saved rule that s3 alone cannot force a label.

transaction.reason: Investigate correspondence using more than color while preserving the source-object anchors. Inspect completion first, then independently distinguish established incomplete progress from established absence of progress. The edited sheet and rounded object are candidates, not verified matches. Unlike the rejected proposal, completion cannot pass for arbitrary paper and a cup, and independently established partial or absent results need not require s1 to fail. Valid uncertainty is not an execution error or grounds to force the reference label.

actions.question: Does the edited image establish that the source paper is stuffed inside the source cup?
actions.criteria: Inspect the edited endpoint directly and compare candidate objects with the source using shape, material, opening geometry, relative scale, and scene context as well as color. Pass only when sufficient correspondence evidence identifies the requested objects and the paper visibly occupies the cup interior in a stuffed placement, rather than lying nearby or on its rim. Fail when visible evidence rules out that endpoint: either the matched objects clearly show an unstuffed placement, or every plausible correspondence supported by the images clearly lacks the required interior placement. Appearance differences alone do not establish failure. Unknown when correspondence, occlusion, or placement leaves completion genuinely possible but unestablished. Describe correspondence evidence separately from interior-placement evidence; do not assess progress here.
actions.binding: The paper and cup remain anchored to the source-image objects. Appearance changes may be compatible with correspondence but do not prove it. Do not substitute unrelated objects or require exact color, printing, or shape preservation.
actions.readout_criteria: Return complete (yes) when s1 passes. Otherwise return partial when s2 passes, because its proposition independently establishes requested progress short of completion; return absent (no) when s2 fails, because its proposition independently establishes no requested progress, including no completion. These s2 alternatives apply even if s1 is unknown. Return unknown when neither alternative is established or valid evidence conflicts. If s2 is skipped because s1 passes, completion is established without s2. Any other skipped or unknown support supplies no negative evidence. Unrelated edits and correspondence alone earn no progress credit.

actions.question: Do the source and edited images establish actual progress toward stuffing the source paper into the source cup while also establishing that stuffing is not complete?
actions.criteria: Independently compare source and edited placement and object correspondence; s1 is advisory, not a prerequisite. Pass only when sufficient correspondence and placement evidence establishes an actual advance toward insertion and also rules out completed stuffing. Relevant evidence can include demonstrable movement into the opening or incomplete insertion compared with the source. Mere proximity, a hand holding paper, or a plausible object match alone is insufficient. Fail only when the images establish that no requested change has progressed, which also excludes completion; do not use fail merely because incomplete progress was not proven. Unknown when correspondence, the change in placement, or the distinction between incomplete and completed insertion remains unresolved. Report the visual basis for correspondence and the comparative placement separately.
